Recommended durable fix: have drop_key_locked RETURN the unwatch descriptor the other two sites already construct (optional<{ISparkMechanism*,string,SparkType}>, populated when running_ && is_event_driven), so a caller cannot silently drop a live watcher.

Add one sentence to the header recording why arm_impl deliberately uses a local pointer-only guard (#2270).

trigger: any path reaching drop_key_locked for a key Guardian already owns (sec-F1 rollback, cs-F1 :632, or the :647 failed-watch teardown)
classification_rationale: layer-up amplification of the engine-side defects
summary: GuardianSparkRuntime holds ONE engine subscription per key shared by N rules (index_->add returns arm_edge only on the 0->1 edge), so an engine-side WHOLE-KEY drop leaves keys_/index_/rules_ intact for every rule. get_status() reports N rules armed, backend_->disarm(sub) is a no-op, and nothing is enforced. Self-heals only on the next apply_rules. This is what turns sec-F1/cs-F1 from an engine bookkeeping bug into a silent Guardian enforcement hole.

trigger: drive the :632 returned-error path (or :653) on a key Guardian owns
classification_rationale: the deferred #2797 defect disables the self-heal for the NEW defects

Server shows the agent caught up; rules stay deaf until an unrelated push. DIRECTLY UNDERCUTS the author's argument that #2797 is safely deferrable: in combination with cs-F1 it converts a transient allocation failure into a durable silent enforcement hole. provenance pre-existing, but newly load-bearing because of cs-F1.

trigger: dedup arm B lands in the window between A releasing mu_ at :613 and A's watch_guarded at :643; A's watch then fails

A commits a fresh key and releases mu_; B dedups and is returned a valid id; A's watch() then fails and :647 drops the whole key, so B's id is silently dead and uncounted. Pre-existing shape (the whole-key teardown predates this PR) and deliberately unnarrowed, but it shares the sink with sec-F1 and any fix should cover it.

summary: Pre-start arms never set watch_armed, so ANY post-commit throw drops the whole pre-start key AND every sibling armed before start(); start()'s replay never sees it. A subset of sparks is silently absent after boot with all counters self-consistent. EXPOSURE E0 - no actor required, this is the boot path - which is a stronger exposure than the E4+E5 recorded for sec-F1 itself.

trigger: any post-commit throw on a deduped Interval/Disk/Startup arm
classification_rationale: timer-tier instance of sec-F1
summary: For Interval/Disk/Startup, mech is ALWAYS null, so watch_armed is ALWAYS false: every post-commit throw on a dedup arm deletes a healthy multi-subscriber timer spark. No orphaned watcher, so ZERO residue - nothing to find afterwards. Generalises sec-F1 beyond event-driven keys.

trigger: a mechanism that emits synchronously on the caller thread inside watch(), plus an inline handler that disarms the same spark type
classification_rationale: UNRESOLVED EXPOSURE - gates pending adjudication per the shared preamble
summary: watch() at :643 runs while holding mech_ops_mu_by_type_. The comment at :618-626 asserts an inline emit re-enters under mu_. A synchronous emit plus an inline handler disarming the same type gives a non-recursive re-lock and a PERMANENT WEDGE in which the rollback can never run. I5(c) state-machine wedge raises to HIGH. E6 is UNVERIFIED: spark_service enqueues, but spark_file and spark_registry were NOT checked. Per the preamble an unresolved EXPOSURE gates pending adjudication and never defaults to no-change. Settling it requires checking whether spark_file.cpp and spark_registry.cpp can emit synchronously from inside watch().

trigger: ~SparkEngine completes while a rollback-driven disarm holds a raw ISparkMechanism* with mu_ released
classification_rationale: referred by unhappy-path to cpp-safety as a lifetime-defect floor candidate
summary: ~ArmRollback -> disarm() captures a raw ISparkMechanism* under mu_, releases the lock, then calls mech->unwatch(). If ~SparkEngine completes meanwhile, mechanisms_ is destroyed and this is a use-after-free DURING UNWINDING. Pre-existing shape for disarm generally, but the rollback adds a new caller reached with a bad_alloc already in flight. unhappy-path referred it to cpp-safety as a policy-floor candidate; cpp-safety did not rule on it because it surfaced after that agent reported.

trigger: sustained memory pressure with the 25s heartbeat retrying an arm that reaches the dedup drop
classification_rationale: unbounded handle growth under sustained pressure
summary: On the throw path the generation is HELD, so the heartbeat retries indefinitely; each retry reaching the dedup drop orphans another OS handle (inotify watch / TP_WAIT / IOCP registration). Bounded only by how long the memory pressure lasts. Requires a SECOND engine consumer since Guardian dedups above the engine, which is why this is MEDIUM rather than HIGH today.

trigger: a chaos or unit test whose phase-1 hook calls back into the engine
classification_rationale: new seam lacks the self-deadlock warning every sibling seam carries
summary: The phase-1 hook fires while mu_ is HELD. Every other seam in this file is placed outside its lock and carries an explicit self-deadlock warning (:741-744); this one has neither. A hook calling arm/disarm/stats/is_running hangs with no timeout. Constrains the design of Gate 5's own chaos harness: phase-1 hooks may only throw.

trigger: stop() concurrent with a rollback-driven disarm on the same mechanism type
classification_rationale: lock-coverage asymmetry newly reachable
summary: stop() never takes mech_ops_mu_by_type_ (only :274/:628/:747/:812 do), so m->stop() runs unserialised against watch()/unwatch() - including the unwatch now reachable from ~ArmRollback -> disarm. Contained today only by mechanism-internal guards (spark_service.cpp:224/:236), which is defence in the wrong layer.

trigger: an orphaned OS watch exists
classification_rationale: no observability for the failure mode the blocking findings produce
summary: Nothing observes an orphaned OS watch. SparkEngineStats has no live-watch count (watcher_units counts MECHANISMS, not watches), and report_fault early-returns when armed_ lacks the key, so armed_faulted and watch_faults_total CANNOT move for an orphan. This is why sec-F1 and UP-1 would be undiagnosable in the field. Recommend a mech_live_watches stat.

trigger: a SECOND SparkEngine consumer arms an equal spec, then another consumer's arm fails into drop_key_locked
classification_rationale: E6 rests on the single-consumer proof, NOT on prefer_spark_
summary: drop_key_locked asserts dropping the whole key is correct. True inside SparkEngine; across components a sibling consumer holding that SubscriptionId is never told, and there is no notification path. Capped LOW by E6 because grep of agents/ and server/ finds exactly ONE production register_consumer (guardian_engine.cpp:1244). Distinct from UP-1, which needs two RULES on one key rather than two CONSUMERS and is therefore NOT capped.

trigger: compiling spark_engine.hpp on a non-libstdc++ standard library

Both assertions are standard-backed. Recorded as contested; cpp-expert's evidence is stronger and this should resolve to refuted once a macOS leg is green.

Confirmed by reading, not inferred: the operator would never know.

trigger: an allocation-pressure throw post-commit racing a concurrent stop(), where the rollback-driven disarm blocks in mech->unwatch()

summary: F3's hard_exit backstop (main.cpp:868-889) polls only guardian_active_io_workers() and runs AFTER agent->stop() (hence spark_engine_->stop()) has returned. spark_engine_->stop() is called directly, unbounded, with no timeout. If ~ArmRollback fires concurrently with SparkEngine::stop() and its disarm() blocks inside mech->unwatch() - e.g. spark_registry's documented WaitForThreadpoolWaitCallbacks(TRUE) drain of a wedged callback, or mech_ops_mu_by_type_ contention against stop()'s un-locked m->stop() (UP-12) - then spark_engine_->stop() never returns and THE F3 SAFETY NET IS NEVER REACHED. I5 raised to HIGH under rule (c), wedges a state machine.

trigger: a dedup arm on a spark key already shared by N armed rules, throwing post-commit into ~ArmRollback's wrong branch
classification_rationale: SOC 2 CC7.1/CC7.2 control citation on the UP-1 defect; concurring, rides on UP-1's gate
summary: Evidence-integrity reclassification. enqueue_lifecycle_locked(...armed...) at :184 correctly fires only on a SUCCESSFUL arm and is ordered after the last throwing step, so a failing attach does not mint a false armed record. But the disarmed entry fires only from detach_rule_locked at :260, which Guardian calls explicitly - and sec-F1's whole-key drop happens INSIDE SparkEngine::arm_impl, a layer beneath Guardian's bookkeeping. So the N-1 already-armed rules lose their OS watch with NO disarm audit entry and NO status transition; their last armed lifecycle record and last-reported compliance state (feeding the audited guardian.device.view endpoint, 365-day retention) stay frozen and silently false. Controls CC7.1 and CC7.2. Note get_status() is a pre-existing fail-closed placeholder reporting every rule errored, so it is NOT the false-assurance vector; the compliance/health outbox stream is.

(3) IT CANNOT GATE UNDER THIS PROJECT'S OWN RULES - ADR-0021 carries no normative prefer_spark requirement, and narrative prose does not qualify as a policy floor, so no agent could ever floor a violation of it. Related: guaranteed-state.md:334 promises operators an upgrading.md entry when the flag flips; none exists.
